chicago_proposed.name: Chicago proposed single-stair ordinance
notes: The five-story limit is the total number of stories above grade, not five stories above a ground floor.
The ordinance also contains sprinkler, corridor, travel-distance, alarm, detection, and door requirements that require design review.
This analytical envelope does not establish that a parcel or design is legally buildable.

illinois_sb4061.name: Illinois SB4061 alternative
notes: The introduced bill describes conditions under which a municipality or county could not prohibit a single-stair building beginning January 1, 2027 if enacted.
This analytical envelope does not establish that a parcel or design is legally buildable.

conservative.name: Conservative opportunity estimate
conservative.description: Uses the smallest observed stair-efficiency gain and spacious unit-size assumptions to avoid overstating unit capacity.
conservative.unit_size_method: Midpoint of the weighted 75th-percentile AHS size range. Chicago renter-occupied multifamily observations are used for zero through three bedrooms; the national sample is used for four and five-plus bedrooms.

median.name: Median opportunity estimate
median.description: Uses the median observed prototype efficiency gain and weighted median AHS size ranges.
median.unit_size_method: Midpoint of the weighted median AHS size range. Chicago renter-occupied multifamily observations are used for zero through three bedrooms; the national sample is used for four bedrooms. Five-plus falls back to the IHDA minimum because the AHS sample is too sparse.

progressive.name: Progressive opportunity estimate
progressive.description: Uses the largest observed stair-efficiency gain and Illinois minimum unit sizes to test the upper bound of compact family-oriented construction.
progressive.unit_size_method: IHDA minimum acceptable new-construction dwelling-unit sizes; two-bedroom assumes one bathroom.

unit_size_evidence.ahs_filters: 2023 PUF; Chicago-Naperville-Elgin CBSA 16980; renter occupied; buildings with two or more apartments; weighted by WEIGHT.
limitations: AHS UNITSIZE is categorical; point estimates use range midpoints and are not measured average square footage.
The national five-plus-bedroom sample is too small for the median profile, so that value uses the IHDA minimum.
These values are capacity assumptions, not architectural plans or market forecasts.

bedroom_reporting.note: Three-plus bedrooms is the headline project measure. Two-plus is also reported because Chicago's ARO uses it as a family-sized reference; four-plus is reported as a larger-family sensitivity.
